items.stem: In Haystack, you need retrieval followed by grounded generation. How is this best expressed?

options.text: As a pipeline that connects a retriever component to a generator component
options.rationale: Correct: Haystack composes components into a pipeline for this flow.

options.text: As a single monolithic function with no components
By calling the generator with no retrieval
By indexing at query time for every request
options.rationale: Indexing per query is inefficient and wrong here.

items.explanation: Correct: Haystack composes components into a pipeline for this flow.

items.stem: Which TWO choices improve search quality in a Haystack pipeline? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Combining dense and sparse retrievers for better recall
options.rationale: Correct: hybrid retrieval often improves recall over one type.

options.text: Choosing a document store suited to the workload
options.rationale: Correct: store fit affects relevance and performance.

options.text: Using one retriever for every query type without testing
options.rationale: One type rarely fits all queries.
Without evaluation you cannot know quality improved.

items.explanation: Correct: hybrid retrieval often improves recall over one type.

items.stem: A Haystack RAG pipeline is about to ship with no evaluation. What is the risk?

options.text: You cannot tell whether retrieval and answers meet quality targets
options.rationale: Correct: without evaluation, quality is unknown and unmanaged.
Lack of evaluation does not break compilation.
Speed is unrelated to the evaluation gap.

items.explanation: Correct: without evaluation, quality is unknown and unmanaged.
